clue.text: Discover by chance how Putin will suffer if wife leaves

indicators.note: to suffer is to be knocked about, so the letters that follow are battered into a new order
the wife leaves, so her letter departs from the word how

explanation.surface: A wry political aside: the Russian president would be hurt if his wife walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if wife leaves' takes W from HOW to leave HO; 'will suffer' then shuffles HO with PUTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit upon something is an idiom for finding it by luck or accident.

clue.text: Pure alcohol's part of how things can go on the Internet

indicators.note: the spirit becomes a component sitting within the other word, so it is placed inside

parts.words: how things can go on the Internet
parts.note: content that spreads rapidly online is said to go viral
gin is a type of alcohol; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A puzzling claim that pure booze is somehow part of online sharing culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' signals the spirit going inside the online word, not a fraction being taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginal describes someone chaste or untouched, a synonym for pure.

clue.text: Time and running order of business

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

indicators.note: running water flows and moves about, so the letters of and are set loose into another order

explanation.surface: A meeting chair speaking of timekeeping and the running order of the day's business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' looks like part of 'running order', but it shuffles 'and' into NDA.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of items, in sequence, to be dealt with at a meeting.

clue.text: Country houses vacated, inhabitants now moving around

indicators.note: inhabitants live within a dwelling, so the shuffled letters sit inside the emptied word
a vacated house is emptied, so only the outside letters of houses are kept
the letters of around are now on the move, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Country homes emptied as their occupants relocate, a picture of rural depopulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country houses' looks like one phrase, but 'Country' alone is the definition; 'now moving' gives ONDURA, which 'inhabitants' sets inside the vacated H_S.
explanation.definitionFit: Honduras is a nation in Central America, bordering Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua.

clue.text: Octane's volatile in the blink of an eye

definitions.text: in the blink of an eye

indicators.note: a volatile substance is unstable and changeable, so the letters of the fuel are rearranged

explanation.surface: Petrol's octane is volatile and can go up in a flash, almost a chemistry fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volatile' rearranges OCTANE; the 's stands for is and is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means immediately, without any delay, just like something happening in the blink of an eye.

clue.text: Defeat Johnson? Why? They say, he's a party pooper

parts.note: to kill a proposal or opponent is to defeat it
Jo Johnson, a Conservative minister and brother of Boris Johnson

indicators.note: what people say signals that a word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: the question word why is pronounced like the letter Y

explanation.surface: A political jibe: why would anyone want to defeat Johnson, when he's the life of the party?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Johnson' seems to mean Boris, but it is his brother Jo, giving JO. 'They say' makes WHY sound as the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy is someone who spoils others' fun, a wet blanket at any gathering.

clue.text: Ministers messing it all up, not a useful thing in office

indicators.note: the word not tells us to leave out the a that follows it

parts.note: someone messing it all up is failing at their task
the senior ministers of a government together form the cabinet

explanation.surface: A jab at a government whose ministers make a mess of everything and are useless in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' drops an A from FAILING to give FILING. The surface sense, a failing cabinet, really is a mocked government; 'in office' is meant as holding power but here means the workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A filing cabinet is the set of drawers for storing papers that every workplace keeps.

clue.text: Even that is a drink!

parts.note: an even surface is a smooth one
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that even this counts as a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothie is a thick blended beverage of fruit, often with yoghurt or milk.

clue.text: Overseeing all bananas and other fruit

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters of the phrase go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of all the bananas and the rest of the produce at a fruit stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like a fruit alongside 'other fruit', but it is slang for mad and shuffles OVERSEEING ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A Seville orange is a bitter variety of citrus grown in Spain and used for marmalade.

clue.text: Press release about to cover that Russian novelist

indicators.note: the reversed word wraps around the other piece, covering it
about here means turned round, so the word for release is written backwards

parts.note: to vent is to let out or release feelings
to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: A publisher's press release covering a famous Russian author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press release' reads as one term but splits in two; 'about' gives TNEV, which 'to cover' wraps round the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a nineteenth-century Russian writer, author of Fathers and Sons.

clue.text: Scottish king to rip off foreign land

parts.note: to do someone is slang for cheating or swindling them

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so the letters of land are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish monarch setting out to plunder some faraway country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' gives NALD. The answer also points at Donald Tusk, cross-referenced from 13.
explanation.definitionFit: Several medieval kings of Scotland bore this name, among them the brother of Malcolm III.

clue.text: Intimidate everyone including servicemen in area around Truro

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so the servicemen go inside the other letters

parts.note: to cow someone is to frighten them into submission
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for servicemen of the navy
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A bully intimidating everybody, armed forces included, somewhere near Truro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts RN inside COWALL: CO-RN-WALL. TRURO is the county town of Cornwall, in the far south-west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornwall is the English county whose only city is Truro, so it is the region surrounding it.

clue.text: Knocking back a pint's fine for one from South Africa

indicators.note: knocking back means drinking, but here it says the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a pint is a typical serving of beer
OK means all right or fine

explanation.surface: A drinker assures us that downing a pint is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' pretends to mean drinking, but it reverses BEER to REEB; the 's stands for is, a link before OK.
explanation.definitionFit: The reebok, or rhebok, is a small grey antelope native to southern Africa.

clue.text: Stress after contract reveals offer from 10?

indicators.note: after says that the second piece is written following the first

parts.note: to flex a muscle is to contract it
tension is mental or physical stress

explanation.surface: Signing a contract brings out stress, a gloomy note on negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is DONALD: Donald Tusk, then President of the European Council, offered the UK a flexible Brexit delay in 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: This coinage named the flexible postponement of Brexit proposed by the European Council president.

clue.text: Ancient Greek pub will open by, ultimately, June 12

parts.note: by, as in measurements like six by four, is the multiplication sign X

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word
the pub opens up the other word, sitting in its middle

parts.note: twelve o'clock in the day is noon
PH, public house, is the abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: A notice that the pub will open by June 12th, with an ancient Greek thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like a date or a cross-reference, but it is twelve o'clock; 'will open' sets the pub inside it, and 'ultimately' takes the last letter of June.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenophon was an Athenian soldier and historian, a pupil of Socrates and author of the Anabasis.

clue.text: In the open air better? Endlessly worse!

parts.note: to better someone is to outdo them

indicators.note: without its ends, only the inner letters of worse are kept

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether outside life is better, and is told it is endlessly worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' strips W and E from WORSE, leaving ORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoors means outside, away from buildings, under the open sky.

clue.text: Mega-publicity is working for US president

parts.note: M is the symbol for mega, the prefix for a million
an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A presidential campaign sees huge publicity machinery working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mega-publicity' reads as one hyphenated term, but splits into M and AD.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth president of the United States and a framer of the Constitution.

clue.text: See 7
Forbid to steal weapon for one serving?

indicators.note: what is stolen is taken in, so the weapon goes inside the word for forbid

parts.note: to ban something is to forbid it
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: A prohibition on stealing a weapon, addressed to someone in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to steal' means take in, so the weapon goes inside the ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman is someone who serves drinks behind a bar; the question mark admits the definition is loose.

clue.text: Men of a certain age essentially ruled out living together

indicators.note: essentially means at the core, so the central words of the phrase are struck out

explanation.surface: Middle-aged men are basically excluded from sharing a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially ruled out' drops OF A CERTAIN, the middle of the phrase, leaving MEN and AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ménage is a household, the people who share a home together.

clue.text: Bishop burnt at stake? In hindsight about time to show forgiveness

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed name goes round the letter for time
hindsight looks backwards, so the bishop's name is reversed

parts.note: Hugh Latimer, Bishop of Worcester, was burnt at the stake in Oxford in 1555

explanation.surface: A martyred bishop, looking back, offers forgiveness to his persecutors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In hindsight' reverses LATIMER to REMITAL; 'about' places it round T. Latimer was one of the Oxford Martyrs burned under Mary I.
explanation.definitionFit: Remittal is a remission, the cancelling of a debt or pardoning of a sin.

clue.text: EU's divided, up in arms about damaging piece

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters are shuffled together
in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: The EU is split and up in arms over something harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives UE, which 'divided' splits either side of the S as 'about' rearranges the letters of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mauser is a German rifle or pistol; piece is slang for a firearm, and a damaging one.

clue.text: Konta regularly represses instincts leading to power grab

indicators.note: to repress is to hold something down within, so those letters enclose the next piece
regularly means taking every other letter of the tennis player's name

parts.note: the id is the Freudian seat of primitive instincts
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Tennis star Konta regularly reins in her instincts before a powerful shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Johanna Konta was the British tennis number one; 'regularly' takes KNA from her name, which 'represses' wraps round the instincts.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap is to seize a person and carry them off by force.

clue.text: Obsessive jerk going after new money from abroad

indicators.note: going after says that the twitch is placed following the earlier pieces

parts.note: the euro is foreign currency from a British viewpoint
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: An obsessive twitch develops as someone chases fresh foreign cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurotic describes someone anxious and fixated, as an obsessive person is.

clue.text: Liberal mangled by two Brexiteers — one's a source of drugs

indicators.note: the Liberal is crushed between the pair, so the letter goes in among them

parts.note: Liam Fox and Michael Gove, Conservative ministers who campaigned for Leave

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician savaged by two Leave campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mangled by' puts L inside FOX GOVE: FOX-G-L-OVE. 'mangled' wants to be an anagram signal, but no letters are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxglove plant yields digitalis, a heart medicine, so it is a natural origin of medication.

clue.text: English composer's daughter taken home

parts.note: Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: An English composer's daughter being brought back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken home' reads as escorted back, but means received as pay, as in take-home pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Money one has earned is what one takes home in wages after work.
